title: Priority Gate: ROI & Risk Scoring for Advisory Requests (batching/caching, quant, routing)
creator: Leah Morrison
description:
Problem: We receive a steady stream of non-bug advisory requests from enterprise customers (batching/caching knobs, quantization profiles, routing policies). Current intake is manual and inconsistent: high-value requests get delayed in a general queue, low-value work consumes SME time, and we lack a clear SLA for 'optimization' advisories. Goal: define and implement a Priority Gate that automatically scores advisory requests on ROI and risk, assigns them to an intake lane (Fast‑Track / Standard / Investigate), and surfaces the minimum evidence required for an approved engagement.

Scope: MVP covers hosted + dedicated advisory requests for performance knobs, KV/prefix caching, quantization readiness, and routing policy changes. It excludes bug reports, security incidents, and full-managed tuning engagements (those will route to Success Engineering).

Acceptance criteria:
- A deterministic scoring rubric that combines 6 signals: estimated token savings, request volume, customer ARR impact, rollback risk, data sensitivity, and engineering effort estimate.
- An automated classifier that assigns one of three lanes: Fast‑Track (<=3 business days SLA), Standard (<=10 business days SLA), Investigate (triage needed; SLA 20 business days), plus explicit escalation triggers.
- Intake form updates in the customer portal with mandatory fields for Fast‑Track: representative prompt samples, baseline cost/latency metrics, and a minimal test harness link.
- Dashboard showing queue counts, SLA burn rate, and top ROI opportunities.
- Playbook for analysts: steps to validate score, when to request a POC, and who to loop in (Research, Runtime, Security).

Design proposal (MVP):
1) Score calculation (weights are configurable via Console):
   - Estimated monthly token savings (40%)
   - Customer ARR / business tier (20%)
   - Request volume (15%)
   - Rollback / correctness risk (10%)
   - Data sensitivity / regulatory constraints (10%)
   - Engineering effort estimate (5%, inverse)
2) Lane thresholds (score 0-100): Fast‑Track >= 70, Standard 40-69, Investigate < 40.
3) Evidence gating: to qualify for Fast‑Track, customer must provide (a) prompt set or sample traffic, (b) current per-call cost or token metrics, (c) a small representative dataset or deterministic prompts for quant checks.
4) Escalation matrix: if security/data sensitivity flag present -> immediate Security review; if rollback risk >= 8/10 -> schedule runtime-side canary and require Dedicated-ops involvement.

Telemetry & instrumentation:
- New tags on advisory tickets: roi_score, lane, evidence_submitted (boolean), sla_deadline, security_flag.
- Dashboard widgets: median time-to-first-response by lane, % of Fast‑Track with validated savings, false-positive rate (recommendation led to <1% regression).

Operational runbook excerpts:
- Fast‑Track flow: PM/Analyst validates evidence (<=8h), assigns Eng SME for quick knob suggestion, ship recommendation template, monitor 72h with guardrail metrics.
- Standard flow: schedule 2-week window for deeper benching, run regression evals, propose quant settings and routing rules.
- Investigate: create scoped discovery epic and estimate.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Over-weighting token savings risks accepting high-risk changes; mitigate with a separate rollback risk floor.
- Requiring too much evidence will reduce funnel throughput; we'll iterate gate strictness after 6 weeks using signal conversion rates.
- Security review adds latency for regulated customers; we propose an SLA tradeoff where security-flagged Fast‑Track still gets a 5-business-day goal if Security can commit a reviewer.

Open questions:
- Who will be the canonical owner of the ROI model? (Product vs. Data Science)
- What is an acceptable false-negative rate (cases where high-ROI requests are misclassified to Investigate)?
- How do we instrument 'estimated monthly token savings' for customers without token telemetry?

Implementation plan (phased):
- Week 1-2: Finalize scoring rubric and required portal fields (PM + Research).
- Week 3-4: Implement intake form changes and tagging in support ticket system; prototype score computation in Data Studio.
- Week 5-6: Console dashboard prototype + routing rules (automation to create lane labels).
- Week 7-8: Pilot with 4 enterprise accounts (Success Eng + Solutions Eng).
- Week 9: Iterate thresholds, ramp to general availability.

Success metrics (first 3 months):
- 60% of accepted advisory requests processed in Fast‑Track or Standard lanes within SLA.
- Median time-to-first-recommendation (Fast‑Track) <= 48 hours.
- Measured savings validated in production for >= 50% of implemented recommendations.

Next steps:
- Product review with Engineering & Security (scheduled 2025-02-17).
- Assign Data Science owner to implement calibration and simulate historical tickets.
- Prepare pilot plan and invite 4 customers for pilot in March.
